name: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for PA-VSD

criteria.description: Complete atresia of the pulmonary valve with no antegrade flow from right ventricle to pulmonary artery
Presence of a ventricular septal defect allowing communication between right and left ventricles
Hypoplasia or absence of main pulmonary artery and/or branch pulmonary arteries
Clinical evidence of central cyanosis in the neonatal period

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pulmonary valve atresia confirmed by imaging and a ventricular septal defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic and cardiac catheterization findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of right-to-left shunting due to pulmonary outflow obstruction
searchTerms: baby with low oxygen skin color

pathognomonic.symptomName: Single second heart sound (loud A2 component)
pathognomonic.notes: Due to absence of pulmonary valve closure

common.notes: Secondary to hypoxemia and heart failure
Due to decreased oxygen delivery and cardiac workload
Chronic hypoxia and increased metabolic demand
Develops over time due to chronic hypoxemia

occasional.notes: Due to turbulent flow across VSD
Due to limited cardiac output and hypoxia

rare.notes: May occur due to ventricular strain or surgical sequelae
Due to paradoxical embolism from right-to-left shunting

searchTerms: backflow of blood in lung valve

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating pulmonary valve atresia and VSD
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography showing pulmonary artery anatomy
Chest X-ray showing decreased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: Association with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in some cases
other: Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment and pulmonary artery anatomy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pulmonary stenosis rather than atresia
Typical four-component defect including overriding aorta and right ventricular hypertrophy

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. 2019.
Maron BJ, et al. Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine. 20th ed. 2018.
Orphanet: Pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect. ORPHA:1207.
